crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Evidence Extraction Tables
children.blurb: Evidence extraction tables are structured summaries used in literature review and evidence synthesis to pull key claims, study designs, populations, interventions, outcomes and effect sizes from individual papers into a comparable grid.

children.name: Weighing the Scientific Consensus
children.blurb: Weighing the scientific consensus means assessing how much agreement exists across published research on a specific question, rather than relying on a single study.

children.name: Questioning Your Own Sources
children.blurb: Questioning your own sources means treating every paper, claim, and model output as provisional until its provenance, method, and conflicts have been checked.

children.name: Deep Research Agents and Landscape Scans
children.blurb: Deep research agents and landscape scans automate the early stages of literature review and evidence synthesis, from finding relevant work to mapping how papers, claims, models, tools, and books relate.

children.name: Translating Between Disciplines
children.blurb: Translating between disciplines means taking findings, methods, or terminology from one research field and restating them so they can be used in another.

sections.body: Literature review and evidence synthesis is the work of turning a pile of papers into a defensible account of what is known. AI systems now read abstracts and full texts, pull out study design, sample, intervention, outcome, and effect size, and place those details into structured tables. They cluster findings by topic, flag contradictions, and draft narrative summaries that a human can check. They also help with broad scans, where a question spans fields and no single search string catches everything. The aim is not to replace judgment but to make the reading load visible and the provenance of each claim traceable. In practice, the useful systems keep a link to the original paper, so a reader can inspect the source rather than trust a summary.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts are genuinely solved at a practical level, and finding papers, deduplicating records, extracting simple fields, and producing first pass evidence tables are now routine for well scoped questions. The site's library holds 135 research papers and 11,795 claims extracted from research works, which gives a sense of the scale that extraction can reach. What is not solved is synthesis under disagreement. AI can show that studies conflict, but it cannot decide which methods were stronger without explicit criteria, and it often misses negative results, unpublished work, and field specific conventions. Deep research agents can scan widely, yet they still hallucinate citations, overstate confidence, and blur the line between a claim in a paper and a claim about the literature. The honest limit is that these tools assist a reviewer who checks sources, they do not certify a consensus.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages in this section follow the path from raw papers to a defensible review. Evidence Extraction Tables covers the mechanics of pulling study details into comparable rows, which is where most reviews begin. Weighing the Scientific Consensus deals with the harder step of judging whether a body of work agrees, and what to do when it does not. Questioning Your Own Sources turns the lens on the reviewer's search strategy, inclusion choices, and possible blind spots. Deep Research Agents and Landscape Scans looks at automated broad searches across many fields, useful for orientation but not for final judgment. Translating Between Disciplines addresses the vocabulary problem, where the same idea carries different names in different literatures, and a reader would go to each page for that specific stage.
